doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Teddy Hill clarified; was there a Detroit drum sound?
summary: They fix the name Teddy Hill and conclude Detroit drummers were all different.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Great, we’re going to have to stop. But before you stop it was Teddy Hill.
Teddy Hill, that’s right, he’s the manager of Minton’s.
Right, oh yeah, because, right, right.

I kind of know what you mean, but I never thought about it, except that I can naively say that I don't think there was a style in Detroit because there was Oliver Jackson, Leon Rice, there was Art, a Caucasian guy, he was a good drummer too...

Art Mardigan, he was good. And there was Elvin, but they were all different...And Roy was different. I don't think there was a "Detroit Sound" but maybe there was a "Boston Sound" but I don't know where Art Blakey falls into all of that.
Pittsburgh! [laughs] and Joe "what’s-is-name" is from there.
Yeah, he doesn't sound like Art.
Oh Kenny Clarke, I loved him.
